articles.title: Wes Henderson Sued: Angel's Envy Co-Founder Accused of Secretly Recording Intimate Moments of Around 40 People
articles.description: Angel's Envy co-founder Wes Henderson faces a civil lawsuit from family members alleging he secretly recorded around 40 people using hidden cameras. His attorney 'unequivocally denies the allegations in the lawsuit'. Wes Henderson, co-founder of the Angel's Envy whiskey brand, Kentucky Bourbon Hall of Fame inductee and owner of the Kentucky Castle hotel in Versailles, is facing a civil lawsuit filed by family members who allege he used hidden cameras to secretly record around 40 people without their consent. The complaint, first filed in Oldham County, Kentucky, claims the recordings were made across several locations, including his private homes and the Kentucky Castle hotel. Henderson has denied the claims through his attorney, and no criminal charges have been publicly reported so far. His attorney said Henderson 'unequivocally denies the allegations in the lawsuit' and added that the defense expects the case to be either voluntarily dismissed or fought hard in court. Wes Henderson Sued Over Alleged Hidden Camera Recordings How The Cameras Were Allegedly Found According to the filing, family members spotted about 15 disguised cameras during a stay at Henderson's Florida home in June 2025. A later search of his Oldham County residence allegedly turned up roughly 15 more recording devices. Nebraska S*x Trafficking Bust: Gujarati Woman Used Hidden Hotel Cameras To Monitor S*xual Abuse of 2 Teenage Girls Live. The plaintiffs claim the memory cards and footage they recovered show people undressing, using the restroom and being intimate. They also allege some cameras were pointed at beds, that cameras were placed inside homes belonging to third parties, and that some clips show s*xual activity at the Kentucky Castle hotel. The complaint further claims there is footage of Henderson himself with other women. Florida Therapist Has Secret S*xual Relationship With Patient, Arrested. Charges Listed In The Civil Complaint The suit lists counts of voyeurism, invasion of privacy, and viewing or possessing depictions of a minor in a s*xual performance. The last count relates to bathroom footage that allegedly features an unidentified person who appeared to be a minor. The plaintiffs also allege that Henderson sent multiple text messages over an 11-month period after being confronted, apologizing and asking for forgiveness. Police Role And Damages Sought The plaintiffs say they handed the recovered equipment and digital recordings to law enforcement. Local agencies, however, indicated they were not actively involved in the civil case. The family is seeking punitive damages, compensation for pain and suffering and medical expenses, and has demanded a jury trial. Who Is Wes Henderson? Henderson co-founded Angel's Envy with his father, master distiller Lincoln Henderson. Bacardi bought the brand in 2015 in a deal reportedly worth about USD 150 million. He was inducted into the Kentucky Bourbon Hall of Fame in 2019, later bought the 53-acre Kentucky Castle property in Versailles and launched the True Story whiskey brand. (The above story first appeared on LatestLY on Oct 03, 2026 07:44 AM IST. For more news and updates on politics, world, sports, entertainment and lifestyle, log on to our website latestly.com).

articles.title: Former WSU Student Receives Maximum Jail Sentence For Secretly Recording Men In Campus Shower
articles.description: The 20 year old former Washington State University student convicted of secretly taking videos of men inside a dorm shower and bathroom has received the maximum jail sentence. Juan Velasco pleaded guilty in August to one count of felony voyeurism in Whitman County Superior Court. Velasco was initially charged with three counts for using his phone to secretly record men in the 3rd floor bathroom of Stephenson South in April of last year. The prosecutor's office dropped two counts partly because two of the victims could not be identified. One victim who was recorded in the shower was identified. Judge Roger Sandberg agreed with the prosecutor's request for the maximum sentence allowed by state law in this case. Judge Sandberg sent Velasco to jail for 3 months, ordered that he undergo a psychosexual evaluation and register as a sex offender for 10 years. The identified victim agreed with that sentencing recommendation. Velasco has been living in Toppenish since he was suspended by WSU. The case was investigating by the WSU PD.

articles.title: 'Peeping Tom gets out': Man who allegedly hid three spy cameras in Hong Kong gym changing rooms out on bail
articles.description: A Hong Kong man who allegedly installed pinhole cameras in changing rooms at a branch of a popular gym chain has been released on bail pending further police investigation to identify potential victims. Construction site foreman Fung Kwok-wang, 34, was not required to answer a count of voyeurism during his first appearance at Sha Tin Court on Tuesday, as prosecutors sought an eight-week adjournment for further police inquiries. Acting Principal Magistrate Cheang Kei-hong granted the defendant HK$2,000 (US$255) bail on condition that he remain in Hong Kong, avoid contact with prosecution witnesses and stay away from the 24/7 Fitness branch on Lek Yuen Street in Sha Tin. The case will be heard again on November 25. The fitness centre reported the case to police on Friday after a customer spotted a small camera secured with black tape in the false ceiling of a changing room. Police combed through the premises and seized three pinhole cameras and three 12GB memory cards from three of the four individual unisex changing rooms. Officers subsequently recovered multiple video clips filmed between September 23 and 25. Fung was arrested shortly after 9pm on Sunday. The Sha Tin district investigation team is handling the case. Voyeurism is punishable by up to five years in prison, which is capped at two years when the case is heard by a magistrate.

pendingReview.title: Man pleads guilty in second hidden bathroom recording case
pendingReview.description: A New Castle County man previously convicted of secretly recording women in a bathroom has again admitted to violating a woman's privacy, this time after prosecutors say he filmed her as she stepped out of a shower inside a St. Georges-area home. Desi D. Turner, 66, pleaded guilty Sept. 28 to a single count of violation of privacy, according to court records. The plea came less than four years after he admitted to similar crimes involving hidden recordings of women at a Newark real estate office. A sentencing date had not been publicly scheduled as of Oct. 1. Recent accusation While at Turner's residence in the 1300 block of Joseph Lane, court records said, a 31-year-old woman went to take a shower in a bathroom that's connected to an unused bedroom in the house. Because the towel rack was broken, court documents said, the woman left her towel in the unused bedroom about 9:30 p.m. on Dec. 24, 2025. She then shut the bedroom door and went to take a shower. After showering, court documents state, the woman entered the bedroom to retrieve the towel. That's where court documents say she noticed "a cellphone propped up on the side table near the doorway of the bathroom with the rear camera facing the bedroom." The woman picked up the cellphone, which was not hers, and noticed it was recording a video. When she stopped the recording, court documents say, she played it back and saw Turner placing the cellphone in the bedroom. Then after a certain amount of time, she saw herself leaving the bathroom naked to grab the towel. She tried to email the video to herself before deleting the recording, according to court documents. The woman learned the video did not transfer because the recording file was too large. The woman returned the phone to where she found it and contacted police, who began investigating. New Castle County police made contact with Turner, who court records say was staying at the Staybridge Suites in Christiana. "Desi stated he had already contacted a lawyer and did not wish to speak to police but handed over his black Samsung cellphone without incident," according to the court document. New Castle County police's Tech Crimes unit was able to retrieve the video, which was about 15 minutes long and corroborates much of what the woman told investigators. Earlier conviction In 2019, a woman discovered a hidden camera at a Patterson-Schwartz office in Newark after it fell out of a toilet paper roll she had picked up. Turner was employed at that office at the time. The woman called the police, documents show. Police were able to identify and contact one other woman who was videotaped, according to court documents. The videos showed the women "using the bathroom with their exposed buttocks visible." The camera's micro SD card led Newark police detectives to Turner. Court documents say he was captured on the video positioning the camera in the back of the stall then quickly leaving. Turner was charged with multiple counts of violation of privacy. Court records show he pleaded guilty on Nov. 28, 2022, to three counts of violation of privacy. In exchange for the plea, prosecutors dropped one count of invasion of privacy and 12 counts of violation of privacy. He was sentenced to one year of probation for each violation of privacy. The sentences, according Superior Court records, ran concurrently, meaning the probations were served simultaneously. Minister When Turner was charged in 2019, he was listed as a bishop at Cornerstone Ministries International in Bear. The church took down its website and Facebook page following his 2019 arrest. A search earlier this year, however, found references online to Turner still being a bishop of the same Bear ministry and conducting a convocation as recently as 2024. The outside of the storefront ministry, located in the Rivers End Plaza, named "Bishop Desi D." as one of its leaders on Oct. 2. A call Oct. 2 to the church went unanswered. An electronic message sent listed on the church website "failed because of a server error." Send tips or story ideas to Esteban Parra at (302) 324-2299 or eparra@delawareonline.com.

pendingReview.title: Bourbon maker accused of secretly filming guests having sex, including at Kentucky Castle
pendingReview.description: Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Kentucky bourbon maker Wes Henderson has been accused by family members of secretly filming them, as well as others in multiple places, including at the Kentucky Castle, according to a lawsuit filed in Kentucky. Henderson is a Kentucky Bourbon Hall of Fame member best known as the founder of Angel's Envy, which was sold for a reported $150 million to Bacardi in 2015. Representatives of Angel's Envy had no immediate response to a request for comment. Later, Henderson purchased The Kentucky Castle in Versailles in Woodford County, a wedding and tourist destination with a hotel and restaurant, and launched a new whiskey brand, True Story, with plans to build a $92 million distillery nearby. Those plans are on hold. What the lawsuit against Wes Henderson alleges In a lawsuit filed in June in Oldham County, family members accuse Henderson of invasion of privacy, voyeurism, and possession or viewing of matter portraying a sexual performance by a minor. A court filing says some underage family members were captured on the cameras nude. Family members did not respond to requests for comment; the Herald-Leader is not naming them due to the nature of the allegations. The lawsuit has been sealed. The lawyers who filed it have not responded to repeated requests for comment about the filing. Henderson denies the allegations On Friday afternoon, an attorney for Henderson issued this statement: "Wes unequivocally denies the allegations in the lawsuit. It is our understanding that the complaint will be voluntarily dismissed. If that does not happen, he is prepared to vigorously defend himself." According to the filing, the family members were vacationing in Henderson's home near Melbourne, Florida, in June 2025 when they discovered multiple hidden cameras, including some capable of live-streaming. They subsequently turned over the cameras and recorded footage to law enforcement, according to the lawsuit. Because the case file has been sealed, any response that has been filed by Henderson was not immediately available. No criminal charges have been filed, apparently. Cameras with Wi-Fi, recording devices found According to the filing, the family members removed approximately 15 hidden cameras and their SD cards and returned home, where they reviewed some of the footage, which captured intimate acts as well as images of themselves in various stages of undress and using the restroom. "The cameras also captured the defendant, Wes Henderson, having sex with other women (not his wife). Upon information and belief, the cameras captured other adults having sex, as well as footage of what appeared to be a homeless individual, potentially a minor, who happened to be carrying a portable medical device, using the restroom," according to the filing. In a footnote, the filing noted, "Some of the videos were from SD cards that captured sex at the Kentucky Castle which is connected to a business interest of the Defendant Wes Henderson." Henderson has owned the Kentucky Castle since 2023. He is facing multiple lawsuits for debts related to his distilling and hospitality businesses. The cameras in the Florida home were disguised as fire alarms, behind a mirror, in a fan, in a clock, in a speaker, in a bathroom air vent directly above the toilet, in charging blocks and plug outlet extenders, according to the filing. According to the filing, "there are a total of 40 people identified as being captured without their knowledge." Some of the footage included Henderson placing the cameras and deliberately placing them to capture views of a bed, according to the filing. More cameras found In the filing, the family members allege they notified other relatives and Henderson's wife, who "gave (them) permission to sweep their Oldham County, Kentucky home for similar hidden recording devices." Allegedly, another 15 similar cameras were found there. The filing also alleges that footage "showed Wes placing cameras in various third parties' homes." Henderson is a deputy coroner in Oldham County and a former firefighter. According to the filing, the footage also showed him wearing a firefighter's shirt while installing a hidden camera. According to the filing, the family members contacted local authorities and turned over the cameras and SD cards from the Oldham County home and the Florida vacation home. "At present, law enforcement continues to maintain possession of the evidence," according to the filing. It is unclear which law enforcement agency has the cameras and footage. Versailles Police Chief Rob Young said he was not aware of the filing. Oldham County Police Chief Greg Smith also said his department is not involved in the case. "After being confronted, and throughout the last 11 months, Wes Henderson has frequently apologized for his actions and requested forgiveness through several text messages to multiple members of his family," according to the filing. The lawsuit seeks punitive damages for pain and suffering, medical expenses, and a jury trial. Unrelated lawsuits were filed earlier this year in Jefferson Circuit Court against TKC Distilling and related companies that produce True Story. Architects Luckett & Farley, which designed the now-shelved distillery, alleged they are owed more than $936,000. And Bourbon Hall of Famer Peggy Noe Stevens alleges her consulting company is owed more than $510,000 for work done. A third lawsuit, filed in June by GMR Marketing, alleges TKC Distilling owes them more than $120,000. All of those lawsuits are still pending.

pendingReview.title: Man accused of filming men in Florida truck stop bathroom caught with sex toys, meth: deputies
pendingReview.description: LEE COUNTY, Fla. (WFLA) -- A man was arrested Thursday after deputies discovered he was filming people in a truck stop bathroom in North Fort Myers. According to the Lee County Sheriff's Office, deputies responded to the truck stop on Park 78 Drive after receiving reports of a suspect filming over stalls in the men's room. Deputies arrived and immediately contacted the suspect, identified as David Floyd, in the parking lot. Deputies searched Floyd's phone and found a video showing him fully naked while sitting inside a restroom stall. In the video, deputies said Floyd held his phone underneath the stall and over it, recording a person in the neighboring stall. Deputies also found other videos on Floyd's phone depicting similar content. Further investigation led to the discovery of Methamphetamine, sex toys, a mask with holes cut into it, and a glass pipe in Floyd's possession. Floyd was arrested for digital voyeurism, possession of a controlled substance, and tampering with evidence.

Representatives of Angel's Envy had no immediate response to a request for comment. Later, Henderson purchased The Kentucky Castle in Versailles in Woodford County, a wedding and tourist destination with a hotel and restaurant, and launched a new whiskey brand, True Story, with plans to build a $92 million distillery nearby. Those plans are on hold. What the lawsuit against Wes Henderson alleges In a lawsuit filed in June in Oldham County, family members accuse Henderson of invasion of privacy, voyeurism, and possession or viewing of matter portraying a sexual performance by a minor. A court filing says some underage family members were captured on the cameras nude. Family members did not respond to requests for comment; the Herald-Leader is not naming them due to the nature of the allegations. The lawsuit has been sealed. The lawyers who filed it have not responded to repeated requests for comment about the filing. Henderson denies the allegations On Friday afternoon, an attorney for Henderson issued this statement: "Wes unequivocally denies the allegations in the lawsuit. It is our understanding that the complaint will be voluntarily dismissed. If that does not happen, he is prepared to vigorously defend himself." According to the filing, the family members were vacationing in Henderson's home near Melbourne, Florida, in June 2025 when they discovered multiple hidden cameras, including some capable of live-streaming. They subsequently turned over the cameras and recorded footage to law enforcement, according to the lawsuit. Because the case file has been sealed, any response that has been filed by Henderson was not immediately available. No criminal charges have been filed, apparently. "The cameras also captured the defendant, Wes Henderson, having sex with other women (not his wife). Upon information and belief, the cameras captured other adults having sex, as well as footage of what appeared to be a homeless individual, potentially a minor, who happened to be carrying a portable medical device, using the restroom," according to the filing. In a footnote, the filing noted, "Some of the videos were from SD cards that captured sex at the Kentucky Castle which is connected to a business interest of the Defendant Wes Henderson." Henderson has owned the Kentucky Castle since 2023. He is facing multiple lawsuits for debts related to his distilling and hospitality businesses. The cameras in the Florida home were disguised as fire alarms, behind a mirror, in a fan, in a clock, in a speaker, in a bathroom air vent directly above the toilet, in charging blocks and plug outlet extenders, according to the filing. According to the filing, "there are a total of 40 people identified as being captured without their knowledge." Some of the footage included Henderson placing the cameras and deliberately placing them to capture views of a bed, according to the filing. More cameras found In the filing, the family members allege they notified other relatives and Henderson's wife, who "gave (them) permission to sweep their Oldham County, Kentucky home for similar hidden recording devices." Allegedly, another 15 similar cameras were found there. The filing also alleges that footage "showed Wes placing cameras in various third parties' homes." Henderson is a deputy coroner in Oldham County and a former firefighter. According to the filing, the footage also showed him wearing a firefighter's shirt while installing a hidden camera. According to the filing, the family members contacted local authorities and turned over the cameras and SD cards from the Oldham County home and the Florida vacation home. "At present, law enforcement continues to maintain possession of the evidence," according to the filing. It is unclear which law enforcement agency has the cameras and footage. Versailles Police Chief Rob Young said he was not aware of the filing. Oldham County Police Chief Greg Smith also said his department is not involved in the case. "After being confronted, and throughout the last 11 months, Wes Henderson has frequently apologized for his actions and requested forgiveness through several text messages to multiple members of his family," according to the filing. The lawsuit seeks punitive damages for pain and suffering, medical expenses, and a jury trial. Unrelated lawsuits were filed earlier this year in Jefferson Circuit Court against TKC Distilling and related companies that produce True Story. Architects Luckett & Farley, which designed the now-shelved distillery, alleged they are owed more than $936,000. And Bourbon Hall of Famer Peggy Noe Stevens alleges her consulting company is owed more than $510,000 for work done. A third lawsuit, filed in June by GMR Marketing, alleges TKC Distilling owes them more than $120,000. All of those lawsuits are still pending. pendingReview.title: Dismissed Skyline High School teacher had a history of alleged grooming, documents show
pendingReview.description: PORTLAND, Ore. (KOIN) -- A high school teacher who was recently removed after the district learned he'd sent inappropriate messages to a student is now appealing to get his job back. But district records show that it wasn't the first time he's been accused of grooming. Eric Rice, 42, who worked as a teacher and assistant coach at Skyline High School in Salmon Creek, Washington, was discharged from his position by the Vancouver Public Schools on Aug. 25, according to a notice of probable cause from the district. The appeal, along with the details of Rice's disciplinary records, was first reported earlier this week by The Columbian. Rice engaged in extensive, late-night direct messaging with a female student over the summer, according to disciplinary records. He reportedly told investigators he exchanged between 50 and 300 messages with the student. The messages progressed from ordinary conversation to questions about her underwear, and even requests for her to send him selfies in her underwear. Clark County Sheriff's Office Sgt. Matt Volker said they investigated the allegations against Rice as well, but no criminal charges have been filed because the student was 18 at the time of the alleged communication. According to district records, Rice initially said he believed the student had already graduated at the time he sent the messages. But district records note that Rice allowed her to spend significant unstructured time in his classroom the year prior, including times when the two were alone together. He also reportedly petitioned her counselor to place her into a senior-year class that was her only class that year, allowed her to walk his dog for six months, visited her at her job and had her at his home. "That you did not first confirm whether [she] had graduated before engaging the text message communication described above does not mitigate your responsibility -- to the contrary, it reflects that you attempted to pursue an intimate, secretive relationship with her which built on the relationship established while she was your student, the moment you believed, incorrectly, that the professional prohibition no longer applied," wrote VPS Superintendent Ricardo Torres-Morales. Rice, who previously taught at Hudson's Bay High School in Vancouver and has been with the district for 18 years, is also accused in several other inappropriate incidents with students. According to the district's records, Rice contacted at least three former students in 2012. In one case, he contacted the former student late at night on Facebook and asked them to pick him up so they could "go somewhere secluded," and attempted to talk her into making out with him. During that investigation, it was also noted that Rice had sexual relations with a student after she graduated in 2011. He reportedly acknowledged his behavior at a meeting with district officials in 2013 and was warned specifically about grooming behavior and boundary violations. When he was turned down for a job as head coach of the girls' golf team in 2015, the district again noted his "evolving pattern of poor decision making" and issued a written directive ordering him to comply with VPS police on staff-student boundaries and technology use. In 2019, the district went even further and permanently removed Rice from coaching any female teams after a parent complained that he used his position to "access and 'groom' female students for future engagement" in a "predatory" manner. That complaint stemmed from additional late-night Facebook and Snapchat messages Rice reportedly sent to another former student and athlete. A spokesperson from the district confirmed to KOIN 6 News that Rice has appealed the termination of his contract, and a hearing is pending. The Washington Office of Professional Practices confirmed it opened an investigation into Rice's conduct in mid-September, and that investigation is ongoing. In late 2024, Hudson's Bay High School came under scrutiny when another of its teachers, Shadbreon Gatson, was arrested and charged with sexual misconduct with a minor. The charge was later dropped due to the expiration of the statute of limitations, since the alleged misconduct took place in 2013. Another VPS employee, custodian James Mattson, was arrested in 2022 after it was discovered he placed hidden cameras in the girl's locker room at Alki Middle School and in the female staff bathroom at Skyview High School. At the time, police said the videos they found dated back to 2013. Mattson pled guilty to 137 counts of voyeurism and was sentenced to 10 years in prison.
